listing.name: Small helper: starsector log filter (Windows)
listing.summary: For those of you that use the log files extensivly:
listing.aiSummary: Filters Starsector log files to show only errors, warnings, and specific mod messages.

descriptionHtml:
For those of you that use the log files extensivly:

save this script for the powershell somewhere:
param(
    [string]$LogPath = "<your starsector folder>\starsector-core\starsector.log",
    [switch]$ClearScreen = $false
)

# Check if log file exists
if (-not (Test-Path $LogPath)) {
    Write-Host "ERROR: Log file not found at: $LogPath" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Make sure Starsector is installed at <your starsector folder> or specify the path." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    
    # Try to find the log file automatically
    Write-Host "Searching for starsector.log..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $possiblePaths = @(
        "<your starsector folder>\starsector-core\starsector.log",
        "C:\Program Files\Starsector\starsector-core\starsector.log",
        "C:\Games\Starsector\starsector-core\starsector.log",
        "$env:USERPROFILE\Games\Starsector\starsector-core\starsector.log"
    )
    
    $found = $false
    foreach ($path in $possiblePaths) {
        if (Test-Path $path) {
            Write-Host "Found log file at: $path" -ForegroundColor Green
            $LogPath = $path
            $found = $true
            break
        }
    }
    
    if (-not $found) {
        Write-Host "Could not find starsector.log automatically." -ForegroundColor Red
        Write-Host "Please specify the path manually: .\starsector_log_filter.ps1 -LogPath 'YOUR_PATH'" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        exit
    }
}

if ($ClearScreen) {
    Clear-Host
}

Write-Host "=== Starsector Log Filter ===" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Watching: $LogPath" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "Showing: strifespark activity, errors, and warnings" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "Press Ctrl+C to stop" -ForegroundColor Yellow
Write-Host ""

# Tail the log file with filtering
Get-Content -Path $LogPath -Wait | ForEach-Object {
    $line = $_
    
    # Check for Mod Lines or Error/Warning Lines based on strict rules
    if ($line -match 'strifespark' -or $line -match ' ERROR ' -or $line -match ' WARN ') {
        
        # Color code the output
        if ($line -match ' ERROR ') {
            Write-Host $line -ForegroundColor Red
        } elseif ($line -match ' WARN ') {
            Write-Host $line -ForegroundColor Yellow
        } elseif ($line -match 'strifespark') {
            # Lines containing mod keywords (assuming they are usually INFO/DEBUG lines we want to see)
            Write-Host $line -ForegroundColor Green
        } else {
            # Fallback for lines that matched one of the three conditions but weren't colored by the specific ERROR/WARN/Mod checks above 
            Write-Host $line
        }
    }
    # All other lines are implicitly ignored.
}

NOTE: My mod is called 'Strifespark' you will need to replace this with your own prefix in the code above!

Now you can use a simple batch script:
@echo off
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0starsector_log_filter.ps1" => if the ps1 file is placed on the desktop, else adapt path.
pause

1. Click the bat file
2. Start starsector
3. All log entries will now be filtered to only show warnings, errors or your mod-specific messages (which are prefixed by starsector by default)
aiDescription: Provides a PowerShell script and batch file to monitor the Starsector log in real-time. It highlights errors in red, warnings in yellow, and mod-specific lines in green, ignoring all other output.
